queries: Claude Code built production custom software impressed February 2026 compiler Nicholas Carlini

sources_considered.why: Read the abstract and submission history to establish the project, attribution and February 23 public availability.
Read passages explaining the previously unfinished ANF verification task, existing CPS template, public proof history, and limitations of attribution.
Material counterevidence: an examined Claude-built compiler contains familiar designs rather than novel compiler ideas.
The compiler's size and functionality alone do not establish substantive differentiation from existing compilers.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract; sections 1 and the discussion of reproducibility supply the comparison and attribution limits
evidence_items.explanation: The report documents Claude Code producing machine-checked verification code for an ANF transformation whose corresponding proof had previously been left as future work. It adapted an existing CPS proof under expert guidance, adding a distinct verified property rather than merely reproducing the template; February 23 dates the public artifact report, not an asserted exact completion day.

evidence_items.locator: Section “What the Claude C Compiler Reveals About AI Coding”
evidence_items.explanation: Lattner's examination supports a narrower claim that this compiler implements known ideas. It neither evaluates the CertiCoq verification artifact nor establishes that Claude Code cannot implement differentiated functionality.

unresolved_gaps: The proof report is a preprint and the attribution to Claude Code is the researcher's account.
The report itself notes that source history cannot conclusively establish AI authorship.
No independent reproduction of the complete generation process was established.
